definitions.gloss: hanging strap; strap handle on trains and buses
definitions.explanation: the hanging loops or handles on public transportation that standing passengers hold onto for balance

examples.japanese: {吊|つ}り{革|かわ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つかまって⟦{立|た}っていた→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: I was standing while holding onto the strap.

examples.japanese: ⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{揺|ゆ}れた→揺れる：01161_yureru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{吊|つ}り{革|かわ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦しっかり→しっかり：01272_shikkari⟧⟦{握|にぎ}った→握る：02383_nigiru⟧。
examples.english: The train shook, so I gripped the strap tightly.
I'm too short to reach the hanging strap.

notes:
FORMS:
{吊|つ}る (to hang) + ⟦{革|かわ}→革：19310_kawa⟧ (leather) → hanging leather

Historically, these straps were made of leather, hence the name. Modern ones are often made of plastic or synthetic materials.
- Triangle-shaped (⟦{三角形|さんかくけい}→三角形：05436_sankakukei⟧) - traditional style
- Ring-shaped ({輪|わ}っか{型|がた}) - common on newer trains
- Priority seat straps - often a different color

ADVERTISING:
{吊|つ}り{革|かわ}⟦{広告|こうこく}→広告：02747_koukoku⟧ (strap advertising) refers to advertisements placed on or near the straps, a common form of train advertising in Japan.

- ⟦{立|た}ち→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧⟦{客|きゃく}→客：00865_kyaku⟧ (standing passenger)
- ⟦{座席|ざせき}→座席：02832_zaseki⟧ (seat)
